newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks slip at open after Dow fall.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks slip at open after Dow fall.

text.p: The Australian share market opened weaker on light volume on Monday after Wall Street continued to fall on increasing concerns about U.S. inflation and the possibility of rising interest rates.
At 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was eight points weaker at 2,260.7.
The June share price index was three points down at 2,258 and at a 2.7 point discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said that although most major stocks were weaker, the bank sector had been hardest hit by selling as investors cashed in some profits.
"Volume has been quite subdued so you can't read much into this market," one dealer from a Sydney brokerage said.
"What I would say however is that the outlook for the bank sector is not as promising as it was say a year ago and investors are now less reluctant to take profits," he said.
Two areas of the market proving to be resilient were the media and paper sectors.

Dealers said News Corp continued to be bought on the back of the phenomenal successful of its blockbuster film 'Independence Day', while Amcor's year profit release this morning was better than some in the market had anticipated.
Amcor shares were up four cents at A$7.78 while News Corp shares were up four at A$6.78.
